title: Detection of Question-Answer Pairs in Email Conversations
abstract: Studies sentence-level question-answer pairing in asynchronous email conversations. The method uses email-thread structure together with lexical and contextual features to identify which earlier question an answer addresses, providing direct empirical evidence for non-adjacent reply alignment in email.

title: Learning to Align Question and Answer Utterances in Customer Service Conversation with Recurrent Pointer Networks
abstract: Directly models question-answer utterance alignment in multi-round customer-service conversations. A recurrent pointer network exploits conversational context and dependencies among alignments and accommodates empty as well as multiple alignments, providing empirical evidence for responses that do not map one-to-one to prior questions.

title: Automatic Question-Answer Alignment for Japanese Diverse Local Assembly Minutes
abstract: Targets meeting transcripts in which a participant may ask several questions together and officials subsequently answer the corresponding questions one by one. A two-stage method segments question and answer material and then aligns corresponding units, explicitly addressing multiple competing prior questions rather than assuming adjacency.
venue: 2024 11th International Conference on Advanced Informatics: Concept, Theory and Application (ICAICTA)

title: Multiple questions in oral proficiency interviews
abstract: Analyzes more than one hundred question/task instances in oral proficiency interviews and documents turns containing multiple questions. It distinguishes different organizations of repeated or multiple questioning and examines how these arise around repair, missing rejoinders, and problematic answers, providing empirical evidence that response scope cannot always be inferred from the immediately preceding question alone.

title: Overview of the NTCIR-16 QA Lab-PoliInfo-3 Task
abstract: Defines an evaluated Question Answer Alignment task over Japanese assembly minutes. The task extracts topical ranges and correspondences between questions and responses in collective-questioning settings where several questions and answers can occur in batches, supplying independently defined gold and formal system evaluation for alignment.
venue: Proceedings of the 16th NTCIR Conference on Evaluation of Information Access Technologies

title: Detection of imperative and declarative question–answer pairs in email conversations
abstract: Extends email question-answer detection beyond interrogative sentences to imperative and declarative forms. The sentence-level model uses content, context, and thread-structure features and is evaluated on benchmark email corpora, making it directly relevant to replies that answer requests or propositions not syntactically marked as questions.

title: Annotating Abstract Pronominal Anaphora in the DAD Project
abstract: Presents an annotation scheme for abstract pronominal anaphora in texts and dialogues. Antecedents may be verb phrases, clauses, or larger discourse segments, and the paper reports inter-coder evaluation, providing empirical support for span-based annotation of proposition-like antecedents.

title: A simple but effective model for attachment in discourse parsing with multi-task learning for relation labeling
abstract: Uses a BERT-based pair encoder to predict discourse attachments while jointly learning discourse-relation labels. Importantly for multi-proposition response scope, the representation permits a discourse node to have multiple parents, an empirically relevant property of multiparty conversation that is lost under single-antecedent tree assumptions.

title: Identifying reference to abstract objects in dialogue
abstract: Reports annotation experiments in which annotators identify antecedents for discourse-deictic expressions as unconstrained regions of dialogue text. Annotators show convergence on the identity of abstract antecedent regions, supporting empirical span-based treatment of propositions and discourse segments instead of restricting targets to noun phrases.
venue: 10th Workshop on the Semantics and Pragmatics of Dialogue (BRANDIAL 2006)

title: Resolving Discourse-Deictic Pronouns: A Two-Stage Approach to Do It
abstract: Presents a two-stage system that first detects discourse-deictic pronouns and then resolves them to verbal or clausal antecedents. The empirical evaluation separates detection from antecedent resolution and demonstrates a computational approach to proposition-like target selection beyond entity coreference.
venue: Fourth Joint Conference on Lexical and Computational Semantics (*SEM 2015)

title: Anaphoric Annotation in the ARRAU Corpus
abstract: Describes anaphoric annotation in ARRAU, which includes task-oriented dialogue among its genres. The representation explicitly permits multiple antecedents for ambiguous expressions and discourse antecedents denoting abstract entities such as events, actions, and plans, making it useful for null, ambiguity, and multi-antecedent modeling.

title: Resolving Discourse Deictic Anaphora in Dialogues
abstract: Presents an algorithm for resolving discourse-deictic anaphora in spoken dialogue. It first distinguishes individual, discourse-deictic, and vague uses of pronouns and demonstratives and then resolves discourse-deictic cases against preceding discourse, with empirical evaluation on spoken-dialogue data.

title: Discourse Structure and Dialogue Acts in Multiparty Dialogue: the STAC Corpus
abstract: Introduces the STAC corpus of multi-party strategic chats annotated with full SDRT discourse structures. The data contain interleaved conversational threads and explicit discourse links between elementary discourse units, supplying empirical material for evaluating non-local response attachment rather than only turn-level dialogue acts.

title: Towards identifying unresolved discussions in student online forums
abstract: Empirically analyzes discussion structures in student online forums to identify unresolved discussions and unanswered questions. The work distinguishes patterns in which questions receive answers from those in which issues remain unresolved, making it relevant to explicit modeling of missing response links.

title: Discourse parsing for multi-party chat dialogues
abstract: Develops a discourse parser for multi-party chat that predicts discourse attachments and relation labels among elementary discourse units. Because the parser must decide which preceding discourse unit a new unit attaches to in threaded and interleaved dialogue, it provides direct computational evidence for response-antecedent selection below the whole-message level.

title: Dialogue Acts, Synchronizing Units, and Anaphora Resolution
abstract: Reports a corpus analysis and a model of anaphora resolution in spontaneous spoken dialogue. The analysis distinguishes nominal antecedents from sentential or discourse-deictic antecedents and from vague cases with no clearly identifiable linguistic antecedent, directly motivating null or unresolved outcomes rather than forced nearest-antecedent attachment.

title: Stay Together: A System for Single and Split-antecedent Anaphora Resolution
abstract: Provides a unified end-to-end architecture for single- and split-antecedent anaphora using predicted mentions, demonstrating how reference resolution can represent both ordinary and multi-antecedent links.

title: Syntax and semantics of questions
abstract: Provides a compositional semantic analysis of questions and their possible answers, establishing machinery that later work uses to characterize when propositions answer or partially resolve a question.

title: Resolving abstract anaphors in Spanish discourse: Underspecification and mereological structures
abstract: Examines abstract anaphora in Spanish where several preceding propositions or eventualities may contribute to the interpretation, using discourse structure and mereological relations to represent complex abstract referents.

title: Information Structure: Towards an integrated formal theory of pragmatics
abstract: Develops a Questions Under Discussion account of discourse organization in which questions structure conversational goals and propositions are relevant insofar as they address the current question under discussion.

title: A Mention-Ranking Model for Abstract Anaphora Resolution
abstract: Formulates abstract-anaphora resolution as mention ranking and learns to score candidate antecedent spans for abstract anaphors, combining neural representation learning with training data derived from shell-noun constructions.

title: End-to-End Neural Discourse Deixis Resolution in Dialogue
abstract: Presents an end-to-end neural model for discourse-deixis resolution in dialogue that identifies discourse-deictic anaphors and their antecedent spans rather than relying on gold anaphor or antecedent boundaries.

title: A Twin-Candidate Based Approach for Event Pronoun Resolution using Composite Kernel
abstract: Treats event-pronoun resolution as selection among candidate verbal event antecedents and learns pairwise preferences between competing antecedent candidates, including cases with no suitable antecedent.

title: Resolving Shell Nouns
abstract: Addresses automatic resolution of shell nouns to the clauses or other textual material that supply their semantic content, treating the problem as locating potentially non-nominal antecedent spans.

title: Resolving questions, II
abstract: Extends the formal theory of question resolution to additional discourse phenomena and clarifies how conversational context constrains what counts as an appropriate resolution of a question.

title: Resolving Event Noun Phrases to Their Verbal Mentions
abstract: Studies resolution of event-denoting noun phrases to earlier verbal mentions across potentially long discourse distances, using lexical, syntactic, morphological, semantic, and positional evidence for antecedent selection.

title: Anaphora With Non-nominal Antecedents in Computational Linguistics: a Survey
abstract: Surveys computational research on anaphors whose antecedents are clauses, sentences, or discourse segments and whose referents may be propositions, events, facts, or situations, covering terminology, annotation, datasets, and resolution methods.

title: Joint Learning for Event Coreference Resolution
abstract: Jointly models event coreference with event anaphoricity determination, providing transferable methods for deciding whether an event mention has a supported antecedent before antecedent selection.

title: The CODI-CRAC 2021 Shared Task on Anaphora, Bridging, and Discourse Deixis in Dialogue
abstract: Defines shared tasks for anaphora, bridging, and discourse-deixis resolution over multiple conversational datasets, including end-to-end identification of discourse-deictic links rather than assuming ordinary entity antecedents.
